A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Visual Instruction Bottleneck Tuning (Vittle). Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original MLLM evaluations, robustness experiments, ablations and representation analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds model-backbone comparisons, memory measurements and response-diversity evaluations.

M1.justification: The bottleneck architecture, IB objective, priors and interpolation are retained. V2 Section 3.3 explicitly uses posterior means at inference, whereas v1 defines sampled posteriors and leaves its inference averaging formula unqualified. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the implemented procedure or clarifies an existing detail.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training datasets and 45-dataset evaluation suite, including the same perturbations and long-tail scenarios. Added backbone and diversity evaluations reuse existing coverage. The new OCR limitation does not document a separate benchmark or test scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated alternative training methods remain standard instruction tuning, LoRA, weight decay, ROSS and LIT. V1 Table 11 and v2 Table 12 retain identical comparator membership. New backbone experiments extend the standard-training versus Vittle comparison to additional model configurations.

E3.justification: V2 Table 6 adds evaluations using LLaVA-Mini-Vicuna7B and LLaVA-Llama3-8B-Instruct. Appendix B.4 introduces peak-memory measurement and evaluates existing LB-COCO responses using Distinct-1, Distinct-2, compression ratio and Rouge-L homogeneity. The previously reported benchmark protocols and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.4 investigates memory overhead and whether bottleneck training compromises response diversity, using Tables 14 and 15. Existing layer, regularization and interpolation ablations, perturbation-severity tests, case studies and representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging GPT-4o judgments over three repeated runs. V2 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or changed uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing matched numerical results and figures are unchanged. New Table 6 reports control/Vittle (F) POPE-shift accuracies of 77.39/78.32 for LLaVA-Mini and 80.54/84.08 for LLaVA++. Tables 14–15 add memory and diversity results, while the conclusion newly reports slight OCR degradation without quantitative results.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix D newly specifies the interpolated posterior's mean and covariance and acknowledges that different posterior distributions enter the two IB terms. Appendix E also connects the deterministic-map proof assumption to posterior-mean inference. The existing IB bounds, EMID proposition and principal proof steps remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain end-to-end IB-based multimodal instruction tuning, its variational formulation and robustness justification, and validation across 30 shift scenarios. Changing the abstract from three to multiple MLLMs reflects added supporting experiments without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the proposed entropy and representation-divergence reductions as tentative. It adds an explanation for unstable bottleneck training and limitations involving conflicting language priors and OCR. Noisy-annotation and domain-generalization caveats already appeared in v1 Appendix F and are retained in the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code URL, explicitly documents posterior-mean inference, and describes peak-memory measurement across eight training GPUs and one inference GPU. Existing hyperparameter tables, training recipes and pseudocode are retained. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly credits Alemi et al. for the output-information bound and adds references concerning probabilistic embeddings, Mixout, posterior collapse, language priors, diversity metrics and additional backbones. Frontier-model references are replaced, while the core research positioning and extended literature review remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted method and theory rewrites, adds experimental discussion, moves and expands limitations into the conclusion, and places the extended literature review before the derivations. Author/header and acknowledgment text also change. The overall narrative and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6, 14 and 15 for backbone, memory and diversity comparisons. Existing tables are renumbered and locally reformatted, and displays move or resize during reflow. All fourteen figures are retained without changed graphical results.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens an already extensive study with additional backbone tests and focused checks of memory overhead and response diversity. More explicit inference information, code-access information and qualified limitations improve transparency. The gains are incremental: existing benchmark results and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, and the newly acknowledged posterior asymmetry is not resolved through a revised bound.
